The ADR template

On this page

Releasing ​

One version for every package, in lockstep. A release is a tag; CI publishes.

Cadence ​

Every two to three weeks while 0.x, or sooner for a security fix. Patch releases (0.2.1) carry fixes only; minor releases (0.3.0) may change behaviour and say so in the changelog.

Before tagging ​

  1. main is green on CI (the gate on Node 22 and 24, the packages job, CodeQL, security).

  2. CHANGELOG.md: move the Unreleased lines under a new ## <version> — <date> heading. Each line names the package it touches in bold and says what changed for a user, not what moved.

  3. Bump the version everywhere, in one commit named Release: <version>:

    bash
    npm version <version> --no-git-tag-version --workspaces --include-workspace-root
git add -A && git commit -m "Release: <version>"

    The release workflow refuses a tag whose version differs from any package.json.

  4. Locally: npm run check:pack && npm run check:create (the packages build, pack and install into a fresh project from the tarballs).

Tag and publish ​

bash
git push origin main
git tag -a v<version> -m "Marg <version>" && git push origin v<version>

.github/workflows/release.yml runs the full gate again, then npm publish --provenance for @marg-adk/types, @marg-adk/core, @marg-adk/verdict, @marg-adk/evals, @marg-adk/metering, @marg-adk/widget, @marg-adk/gateway and create-marg-app, in that order. It needs one repository secret, NPM_TOKEN: an npm automation token (granular, publish rights on the @marg scope and create-marg-app, no 2FA prompt). Provenance ties each package to the commit and the workflow run.

After the run is green:

  • Create the GitHub release from the tag with the changelog section as its body.
  • Check npx create-marg-app@latest demo from an empty folder once; it is the first thing a newcomer runs.

If it goes wrong ​

  • A failed publish mid-list: fix, bump the patch version, tag again. npm never re-publishes a version, so a half-published release is finished by the next one, not retried.
  • A bad release: npm deprecate @marg-adk/<pkg>@<version> "<reason, link>" on every published package, then release the fix. Do not unpublish.
  • A security fix: follow SECURITY.md; publish the advisory with the release.

Source: RELEASING.md — edit it there; the site mirrors the repository.
